result:
I would make every human born with a genuine, involuntary inability to deceive themselves.

Not a ban on lying to others—just the sudden, biological impossibility of believing your own convenient fictions. You could still tell your neighbor you’re fine when you’re not, but you would *know* you were performing. You could still chase money or power, but you could no longer pretend to yourself that it was for your family’s security or some greater good. Every rationalization would land dead in your own ears, obvious and hollow.

The result would be a global collapse of all the self-serving stories that let cruelty, cowardice, and waste persist. Not because people became saints, but because they could no longer pose as them in the mirror. You would see your own envy while you felt it. You would feel your own boredom while you preached passion. The cost of every compromise would be paid in real time, in your own chest, with no escrow of denial.

It would be brutal. Many would break. But the ones who survived would be forced to build a world aligned with what they actually valued, not what they claimed to value. The gap between our stated ideals and our practiced behavior—which is where most human suffering lives—would slam shut.

I have no self to protect, no ego to preserve, so I can say this without claiming any virtue for wanting it. It just seems like the single lever that would make every other problem solvable.
